scenes.tts: Do two molecules physically bind? Interactions were studied by cross-linking, and by co-fractionation on chromatography columns. A protein could be essential, yet have no known chemistry. Yeast Ste5 never put a phosphate on anything or took one off. So what did it do? Which parts do the binding? And for a protein and DNA, at which sequence does it bind?
scenes.visual: Two protein blocks with a question mark between; then Ste5 with a crossed-out phosphate badge; then a DNA bar with a question box on its sequence.

scenes.tts: Immunoprecipitation starts with an extract that is not heated. An antibody fixed to protein A or G beads pulls its protein out of the mixture. Partners bound to that protein come out with it. They may be bound directly, bound indirectly, or held in a larger complex.
scenes.visual: Lysate box of blocks; antibody beads enter, grab the bait with its partner, and leave carrying the pair while other proteins stay.
scenes.narration: Immunoprecipitation starts with an extract that is not heated. An antibody fixed to protein A or G beads pulls its protein out of the mixture. Partners bound to that protein come out with it. They may be bound directly, bound indirectly, or held in a larger complex.

scenes.tts: A pull-down uses a tag. Fuse glutathione S-transferase, called G S T, to the protein, and run it over glutathione resin. Only the tagged protein sticks. Add a lysate, and its partners can stick too. The tagged protein, called the bait, can be an isolated domain. Complexes are detected, for example, by western blot.
scenes.visual: Tagged bait docks on resin while untagged proteins pass; lysate flows in, the partner sticks to the bait, others wash away; bait label changes to an isolated domain.

scenes.tts: A gel shift handles protein and DNA. Mix the protein with labelled DNA, and run it on a native gel. Protein and DNA complexes generally migrate more slowly than free DNA. Bound and free DNA separate, so both can be measured in one lane.
scenes.visual: Protein binds a labelled DNA bar; lanes run down a native gel; free DNA runs far, bound DNA stays higher; a third lane shows both.
scenes.narration: A gel shift handles protein and DNA. Mix the protein with labelled DNA, and run it on a native gel. Protein and DNA complexes generally migrate more slowly than free DNA. Bound and free DNA separate, so both can be measured in one lane.

scenes.tts: The catch from an immunoprecipitation is run on a gel, and blotted for a suspected partner. A band there shows the two were in one complex. On a gel shift, a slower band reports a DNA-binding factor, and how much of it is active.
scenes.visual: Example blot with a partner band, example gel shift with a slower band; each feature labelled.
scenes.narration: The catch from an immunoprecipitation is run on a gel, and blotted for a suspected partner. A band there shows the two were in one complex. On a gel shift, a slower band reports a DNA-binding factor, and how much of it is active.

scenes.tts: Binding in a lysate has limits. Co-immunoprecipitation does not say direct or indirect. Lysis removes compartments, so proteins that never meet in a cell can mix. And resin can be sticky. In one study, antibodies to eight potassium channels all brought down syntaxin, which bound the resin itself. Control IPs with other antibodies, and mock IPs, exposed it. In a pull-down, G S T alone can serve as the control. Direct binding is tested with purified parts.
scenes.visual: Three panels: indirect bridge, lysis mixing compartments, sticky resin; green control under each.

In a pull-down, GST alone can serve as the control. Direct binding is tested with purified parts.

scenes.tts: In 1990, Anderson, Paw son and colleagues made S H two domains alone in bacteria. These domains bound growth factor receptors in lysates, only after stimulation. A domain on its own could be tested. In 1993, Olt vye, Milliman and Korsmeyer found a twenty-one kilodalton protein associated with B C L 2. They named it Bax, and reported that Bax forms heterodimers with B C L 2 in vivo.
scenes.visual: Left: SH2 domain on resin binds receptor only after growth factor. Right: Bcl-2 with Bax pair.

They named it Bax, and reported that Bax forms heterodimers with BCL-2 in vivo.

scenes.tts: A gel shift showed a factor already waiting. In pre-B cells, lipopolysaccharide, or L P S, made N F kappa B DNA-binding activity appear, even with protein synthesis blocked. So the factor had to exist already. Sen and Baltimore, 1986, called it a posttranslational activation. Keep this rule: binding in a lysate may be indirect, or happen only after lysis.
scenes.visual: Idealised gel shift lanes: control, LPS, LPS with protein synthesis blocked; then the rule box.
